# Ukraine–U.S.–Russia: where is the negotiation track headed?

Zelensky’s visit to New York highlighted three tracks for further diplomacy on ending the war

*During the high-level week of the UN General Assembly, statements were made that underscored the fundamental contradiction in the current negotiation track: Washington is seeking to reach at least some kind of agreement, Kyiv says it is ready for reciprocal steps, while Moscow publicly refuses even to agree to a pause in hostilities.*

*Each side is pursuing very different objectives. The White House is primarily concerned about the prospect of a setback for the president’s party in the midterm elections and is therefore seeking some successes on the international front. Ukraine, understandably, wants the war to end on terms that are as fair as possible. What the Kremlin wants is also clear, but its demands are by no means matched by its capabilities. Moscow is therefore currently seeking to find the path that best serves its interests, while simultaneously trying not to exhaust the resources it needs to sustain the war and to prevent further escalation of U.S. pressure.*

*Donald Trump’s latest statements and his contacts with Volodymyr Zelensky, as well as the progress of Lindsey Graham’s sanctions bill, have seriously alarmed the Putin regime. # Ukraine's top-secret weapon in the counter-offensive stunned Russia.

The Ukrainian 3rd Corps used intelligence and reconnaissance to pinpoint Russian command centers, then deployed suicide ground robots to attack, aiming to disrupt command and communication systems and cause panic within enemy ranks, Euromaidanpress reported.

![Báo Dn Việt](https://vphoto.vietnam.vn/thumb/48x48/vietnam/resource/IMAGE/2025/1/21/6651aa8bec804737aad9143519a40dd9)Báo Dn Việt•25/09/2026

---

![](https://i.ex-cdn.com/danviet.vn/files/content/2026/09/25/robo-2036.png)

Photo of the 3rd Army Corps of [Ukraine](/en/tag/ukraine "Ukraine") / Telegram

In the counteroffensive codenamed Vivaldi, the Ukrainian 3rd Corps deployed suicide ground robots to Russian command posts that had been previously identified by reconnaissance forces.

An intelligence officer from the corps revealed to Radio NV that the goal of the raids was to disrupt command and control, forcing Russia to deploy more troops to protect command centers instead of sending them into combat.

In parallel with the attack on the command center, the intelligence operation also uncovered a diesel pipeline supplying approximately half of the daily fuel needs of Russian forces across the entire operational front.
